```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
suppressMessages({library(dplyr); library(knitr); library(mysterycall)})

# Same output directory and same CSVs the manuscript reads. Nothing here is
# recomputed: a supplement that derives its own numbers is a second source of
# truth, which is the failure the claims table exists to prevent.
OUT <- "mysterycall_outputs"
rd  <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(OUT, f), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

d     <- rd("labubu_cleaned_analysis.csv")
cdom  <- rd("caller_dominance_by_scenario.csv")
covl  <- rd("caller_overlap_by_contrast.csv")
crat  <- rd("caller_rates.csv")
miss  <- rd("missingness_by_arm.csv")
strb  <- rd("strobe_checklist.csv")
dups  <- rd("duplicate_practice_scenario_calls.csv")
rpat  <- rd("restriction_checkbox_by_caller.csv")
devs  <- rd("protocol_deviation_cells.csv")

tf   <- function(x) x %in% c(TRUE, "TRUE", "True", 1, "1")
inc  <- d[tf(d$analytic_inclusion), ]
N_INC  <- nrow(inc)
N_WAIT <- sum(tf(d$analytic_inclusion) & !is.na(d$business_days) & d$business_days >= 0)

# Identical to the manuscript's helpers. Duplicated deliberately rather than
# recomputed a second way: the supplement must print the same digits as the
# paper, so it uses the same package call over the same denominator.
pci <- function(data, var, digits = 1) {
  tb <- as.data.frame(mysterycall::mysterycall_prevalence_ci(data, var = var))
  r  <- tb[tb$category %in% c("TRUE", "1"), ][1, ]
  if (nrow(r) == 0 || is.na(r$proportion))
    return(sprintf("0.0%% (0/%d)", nrow(data)))
  sprintf("%.*f%% (95%% CI %.*f-%.*f%%; %d/%d)",
          digits, 100 * r$proportion, digits, 100 * r$ci_lower,
          digits, 100 * r$ci_upper, r$n, r$total)
}
svc <- function(v) pci(inc, v)
```

This supplement contains material referenced in the main text. It is generated
from the same analysis outputs as the manuscript; no number here is
independently recomputed.

## Appendix Table S1. Caller concentration and contrast separability

Each scenario arm was dominated by a different caller, so a scenario contrast is
also a caller contrast. The second table shows which contrasts have any caller
placing calls under both scenarios; a contrast with zero such callers cannot be
separated from a caller effect by any adjustment.

```{r S1a}
kable(cdom |> transmute(
  Scenario                 = scenario,
  `Calls placed`           = n_calls,
  `Largest single caller`  = top_caller,
  `Their share of the arm` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", top_caller_n, top_caller_pct)),
  caption = "Table S1a. Concentration of each scenario arm in a single caller.")
```

```{r S1b}
kable(covl |> transmute(
  Contrast                      = contrast,
  `Callers placing both`        = n_callers_with_both,
  `Which callers`               = callers,
  `Calls contributed`           = n_calls,
  `Separable from caller?`      = ifelse(n_callers_with_both == 0, "No", "Partly")),
  caption = "Table S1b. Caller overlap by contrast.")
```

```{r S1c}
kable(crat |> transmute(
  Caller                  = caller,
  `Calls placed`          = n_calls,
  `Reached a live office` = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct_reached),
  `Offer-eligible calls`  = n_offer_eligible,
  `Appointment available` = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct_offered)),
  caption = "Table S1c. Call volume and outcome rates by caller. Rates vary widely across callers, which is why a scenario arm dominated by one caller cannot be read as a scenario effect.")
```

## Appendix Table S2. Documentation completeness by caller scenario

Documentation completeness differed by arm in the same direction as the
exploratory outcome. Because the derived availability outcome is read off the
appointment date, a call recorded less completely is scored as less available
regardless of what the practice said. Differential documentation and
differential availability cannot be separated in these data.

```{r S2}
kable(miss |> transmute(
  Scenario              = scenario,
  `Calls placed`        = calls_placed,
  `No call date`        = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", no_call_date, pct_no_call_date),
  `Reached staff`       = reached,
  `No appointment date` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", no_appt_date, pct_no_appt_date)),
  caption = "Table S2. Documentation completeness by caller scenario.")
```

## Appendix Table S3. Reproductive services offered, numeric detail

Numeric detail underlying Figure 1, among the `r N_INC` calls that reached staff
and completed the service interview. Intrauterine insemination and in vitro
fertilization each rest on a single practice; those two intervals should be read
as an upper bound on availability rather than as stable rates.

```{r S3}
kable(data.frame(
  `Reproductive Service` = c(
    "Cycle tracking", "Hormonal labs / fertility timing", "Ovulation induction",
    "Intrauterine insemination (IUI)", "In vitro fertilization (IVF)",
    "Works with donor sperm"),
  `Proportion Offered (95% CI)` = c(
    svc("service_cycle_tracking"), svc("service_hormonal_timing"),
    svc("service_ovulation_induction"), svc("service_iui"),
    svc("service_ivf"), svc("donor_sperm_yes")),
  check.names = FALSE),
  caption = sprintf("Table S3. Reproductive services offered (N = %d calls reaching staff).", N_INC))
```

## Appendix Table S5. Duplicate practice-scenario calls and their adjudication

The protocol specifies one call per practice per scenario. Eight cells contained
two. Where a contact attempt (voicemail, wrong number, abandoned or over-long
hold) preceded a completed call, the completed call determined the cell. Where
two protocol-valid completed calls existed, the cell was treated as a protocol
deviation and excluded from the primary paired analysis rather than resolved by
preferring the earlier or later call. Practice identifiers are redacted.

```{r S5a}
# practice_key holds real practice and individual clinician names. This is a
# secret-shopper study: the people called did not consent to being named, and
# this file is a public submission artifact. Join to the numeric study ID and
# never print the key.
kable(dups |>
  transmute(
    `Record ID`          = record_id,
    `Practice ID`        = practice_id,
    Scenario             = scenario,
    `Call date`          = call_date,
    Disposition          = exclusion_reason,
    `Analytic inclusion` = analytic_inclusion),
  caption = "Table S5a. All calls in a practice-scenario cell containing more than one call. Practices are identified by study ID only.")
```

```{r S5b}
kable(devs |> transmute(
  `Practice ID`         = practice_id,
  Scenario              = scenario,
  `Completed calls`     = n_completed,
  Disposition           = "Excluded from the primary paired analysis as a protocol deviation"),
  caption = "Table S5b. Cells with two protocol-valid completed calls. Practices are identified by study ID only.")
```

## Appendix Table S6. Restriction checkbox, why it is excluded

The instrument's three "restrictions to the individuals you would provide care
to" checkboxes are excluded from every analysis. The codebook defines a ticked
box as a restriction applying to that group, with no field note or branching
logic, but the recorded responses follow two incompatible conventions keyed to
the person completing the form. One caller ticked all three boxes on most of
her entries, which under the codebook definition would mean those practices
serve no one. Every other caller ticked only the box matching the scenario they
called as, which echoes the assignment rather than describing the practice.
Because the convention belongs to the caller rather than the response, and a
quarter of calls record no caller, no recoding rule can separate them.

```{r S6}
kable(rpat |> transmute(
  Caller          = caller,
  `Boxes ticked`  = boxes_ticked,
  Calls           = n),
  caption = "Table S6. Combination of restriction boxes ticked, by person completing the form.")
```

## Appendix Figure S1. Wait time to first available appointment

Restricted to the `r N_WAIT` calls with an observed appointment date. Panels are
a raincloud plot, a ridgeline density, the empirical cumulative distribution, and
within-practice paired differences. These estimates condition on having been
offered an appointment and are descriptive; see Limitation 5 in the main text.

```{r S1fig, out.width="100%", fig.cap="Figure S1. Wait time to first available appointment by caller scenario."}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(OUT, "figures", "fig_panel_wait_times.png"))
```
